correctness.rationale: For any positive-definite quadratic form \(q\), averaging \(q\) over the eight sign/swap isometries preserves the same lower and upper comparison constants against \(N_\beta^2\) and yields \(c(x^2+y^2)\); hence no tilted ellipse improves the Euclidean pullback. On \(x^2+y^2=1\), \(N_\beta^4=1+2(\beta-1)s\) with \(0\le s=x^2y^2\le1/4\), so the extrema are exactly at axes and diagonals and give the two branches. Endpoints \(\beta=0,1,3\) and representative interior parameters were independently replayed.

final_claim: For \(N_\beta(x,y)=(x^4+2\beta x^2y^2+y^4)^{1/4}\), \(0\le\beta\le3\), the Euclidean Banach--Mazur distance is \((2/(1+\beta))^{1/4}\) for \(0\le\beta\le1\) and \(((1+\beta)/2)^{1/4}\) for \(1\le\beta\le3\), with a scalar Euclidean quadratic form globally optimal.
